$comment: Exact versions of everything vendored into a build. Committed; the
binaries themselves never are - CI builds them from these pins and
uploads them as artefacts. Changing a pin is a pull request with a
reason, and it re-runs the parity check in docs/adr/spikes/loom-native.md.

loom.note: Head of master on 2026-09-07. The published maps were built from an unpinned master build; the spike checks whether that output matches this commit.

loom_windows_port.note: MSYS2/UCRT64 build scripts and compatibility patches for Windows.

loom_windows_static.note: The libraries the Windows LOOM tools link statically from MSYS2 UCRT64's packages, which the loom-windows job installs at whatever MSYS2 ships that day: zlib and bzip2 (in topo, loom and octi, by their version strings in the tools of build run 34750505248), besides GCC's runtime and mingw-w64's CRT and winpthreads, whose notices are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. MSYS2 builds each package from the upstream release tarball with patches of its own, so both are pinned: the loom-windows job refuses a package whose revision is not `msys2_revision`, then fetches MSYS2's source package for that revision (its PKGBUILD, patches and the upstream tarball), checks it against `msys2_source.sha256`, verifies its signature with the shared signed() against the key with `msys2_source.signing_key.fingerprint` (fetched at run time; pacman-key cannot be used, since it needs write access to the runner's keyring), and records the exact package revisions. Both source packages' signatures were made on 2026-09-13's revisions by 5F944B027F7FE2091985AA2EFA11531AA0AA7F57, checked that day to be in msys2.gpg of msys2-keyring 1~20260814-1, which pacman trusts through MSYS2's master keys; a new revision signed by another MSYS2 key needs the fingerprint moved with it. The loom-source job, which the LOOM builds wait for, fetches the upstream release tarball, checks its sha256, and verifies its signature against the key with the primary fingerprint recorded here, each checked on 2026-09-13 to be the key that made the published signature (zlib's is Mark Adler's, as for FFmpeg's zlib; bzip2 1.0.8's was made by a subkey of Mark Wielaard's).

engine.note: The same bytes on every machine. At v0.8.3 every text file the engine reads or writes is UTF-8 with LF, the service day is formatted without %-d or the locale's names, and --schema writes its bytes past the console's text layer, so a Windows sidecar can build a map, plan an export and print the schema the fingerprint below was taken from (E19; engine issue 22). Before it, v0.8.2 made map.build's line_order a preference rather than a whitelist (A4-02, engine issue 28). Additive at protocol 1 and the schema is byte-identical, so the tag is the gate. The handshake compares version and protocol with engine.info and refuses any other; the vendoring job installs the package at the tag.

python.note: Upstream publishes no checksum manifest and no per-asset .sha256, so these hashes were computed on first download and are what every later build is checked against. A changed hash means the asset changed, which is the point.

python.licence_check: Verified 2026-09-07: the interpreter links libedit, not GNU readline, and _dbm links only libSystem - no GDBM. Both are GPL components that must stay out; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. The Windows asset, listed 2026-09-12, has no readline and no _dbm or _gdbm extension; darwin-x64 has the same names as darwin-arm64.

licence_texts.note: The licence texts the runtime owes (issue 108, ADR-042). The install_only asset carries CPython's LICENSE.txt only; each target's `full` archive, the same build before python-build-standalone repackaged it, carries a `licenses/` folder and PYTHON.json, whose build metadata names the licence file of each extension module's linked libraries. scripts/vendor-python.sh fetches the full archive, checks `full.sha256` (computed on download on 2026-09-13 and matching the digest GitHub records for the asset), extracts only `licenses/` and PYTHON.json, and ships both under the runtime; scripts/check-vendored.mjs then requires the metadata, the folder and three reviewed lists per target to agree, in the vendor job and again at packaging. `unlisted`: texts owed that the metadata names for nothing, each with the file it is compiled into and strings that prove it, looked for in that file on every run. A version in `contains` is written as the C string it is in the binary, between NUL characters (\u0000), so a later version that merely begins with it (1.3.2.1) does not pass. `named_absent`: texts the metadata names that the archive does not carry, each with why nothing is owed. `not_linked`: texts carried that no extension names. Every text named must be carried or be named_absent; every text carried must be named, unlisted or not_linked, once; and every entry must still be true. A new python-build-standalone release therefore fails the job until a person rereads these lists against the new metadata: that is the intended cost. Measured in specs/027-licences/research.md.

cpython_incorporated.note: CPython's Doc/license.rst at the pinned version's tag: its 'Licenses and Acknowledgements for Incorporated Software' (HACL*, BLAKE2, SipHash, dtoa, asyncio's and the other notices) are not in the LICENSE.txt the runtime ships. Fetched by commit, checked against sha256 (computed on download on 2026-09-13), and shipped as `file` inside the runtime's licenses folder.

ffmpeg.note: Built in this repository by scripts/vendor-ffmpeg.sh, in the ffmpeg jobs of .github/workflows/vendor.yml, natively on each target (ADR-040, amending ADR-012): ffmpeg and ffprobe only (the engine finds ffprobe beside SCHEMATIC_FFMPEG by name). FFmpeg from its release tarball, x264 from a commit, both checked by sha256 before use; x264 is the only external library, and zlib, which the PNG codecs need, is the operating system's on macOS and Linux and built statically from its release tarball on Windows, which has none. `source.sha256` was computed on download on 2026-09-13 (FFmpeg publishes a GPG signature, not a checksum); the --sources job verifies that signature, and zlib's, with gpg against keys fetched at run time and trusted only for the `signing_key.fingerprint` recorded here (FFmpeg's release signing key, and Mark Adler's, zlib's maintainer), each checked on 2026-09-13 to be the key named inside the published signature. `x264.sha256` is of the uncompressed tar `git archive --format=tar --prefix=x264-<commit>/` writes for the commit, which is byte for byte the tar inside VideoLAN GitLab's .tar.bz2 of it; `x264.commit` is master's head since 2025-09-10, and the commit BtbN's builds pin. `zlib.sha256` matches the digest GitHub records for the release asset. Per target: `configure` is FFmpeg's configure line exactly as `ffmpeg -version` prints it; `x264_configure` and `zlib_configure` are the arguments given to each configure besides `--prefix`, which names the build's own dependency folder; `reports` is the token after 'ffmpeg version '. The script refuses to build when the lines it composes differ from these, and the proof refuses a binary whose -version differs.
ffmpeg.licence: GPL-3.0-or-later: every target is configured --enable-gpl --enable-version3 and links x264 (GPL-2.0-or-later); none is --enable-nonfree

source.licence: LGPL-2.1-or-later, GPL-2.0-or-later with --enable-gpl, and the version 3 of each with --enable-version3

electron_ffmpeg.note: The FFmpeg library Electron ships inside the app (libffmpeg.dylib in Electron Framework.framework/Versions/A/Libraries/ on macOS, ffmpeg.dll beside the executable on Windows): Chromium's media decoder, which the app never calls itself and which is not the ffmpeg above (ADR-043, issue 109). Electron builds it from Chromium's copy of FFmpeg with its release gn args (`ffmpeg_branding = "Chrome"`, `proprietary_codecs = true` in build/args/all.gn; `is_component_ffmpeg = true`, `is_official_build = true` in build/args/release.gn) and one patch of its own to FFmpeg's BUILD.gn. Everything is pinned by git object id, so nothing depends on an archive's bytes: googlesource's +archive tarballs carry the download time and differ from one fetch to the next, but the tree they unpack to does not. The electron-ffmpeg-source job refuses a run whose package-lock.json installs another Electron than `electron.version`, checks that Electron's DEPS at `electron.commit` names `chromium.version` and that `electron.tag` still names that commit, that Chromium's DEPS at `chromium.commit` names `ffmpeg.commit` as its ffmpeg_revision and that `chromium.tag` still names that commit, fetches FFmpeg at its commit, each Chromium directory at `chromium.commit` and each of `chromium_deps` at the commit Chromium's tree records for it, and refuses any whose tree id is not the pinned one, both as unpacked and as gitiles lists it at that commit, and each Electron file whose blob id is not. `chromium_trees` and `chromium_deps` are what FFmpeg's BUILD.gn and the files it imports name outside itself (`//build`, `//third_party/opus`, `//third_party/nasm` for the x86-64 assembly, `//tools/generate_stubs` for the Windows exports), with `media/ffmpeg`, whose scripts generate its configuration; `electron_files` holds Electron's FFmpeg patch, its release gn args, and the eight patches in Electron's patches/chromium/ that change files under build/ (each listed in its .patches, checked on 2026-09-13 for Electron 44.2.0 and again on 2026-09-14 for 44.3.0, whose .patches adds three patches that change nothing under build/, third_party/ffmpeg/, third_party/opus/, third_party/nasm/, media/ffmpeg/ or tools/generate_stubs/), with that list. An Electron bump moves this whole block: the Chromium version and commit from Electron's DEPS at the new tag, the FFmpeg commit from Chromium's DEPS, and every tree and blob id (`git rev-parse <commit>^{tree}` for FFmpeg; gitiles' `?format=JSON` listing of each directory at the Chromium commit, which for a DEPS entry such as third_party/nasm gives its repository and revision; `gh api repos/electron/electron/contents/<path>?ref=<tag> --jq .sha` for Electron's files). Measured on 2026-09-13 from Electron 44.2.0's own zips, without running them: `FFmpeg version git-2026-07-15-6cfe2122b0` and `libavcodec license: LGPL version 2.1 or later` in the Mac library, and the 29 components under `components` in its symbol table and in Chromium's config for chromium/config/Chrome/{mac,win}; CONFIG_GPL, CONFIG_NONFREE and CONFIG_VERSION3 are 0 there. Moved to Electron 44.3.0 on 2026-09-14: its DEPS names Chromium 152.0.7977.78, whose DEPS names the same FFmpeg commit and whose build, media/ffmpeg, third_party/opus, tools/generate_stubs and third_party/nasm are the same trees as 152.0.7977.76's; of Electron's files only patches/chromium/.patches changed; and the darwin-arm64 libffmpeg.dylib npm installs for 44.3.0 is the same size as 44.2.0's, 2,317,968 bytes though not the same bytes, reports the same version and licence, and holds the same 29 components, read without running it.

build.what: Chromium's GN build configuration, which BUILD.gn imports (//build/config/...)

media/ffmpeg.what: Chromium's scripts that run FFmpeg's configure for each branding and target and generate ffmpeg_generated.gni and chromium/config (scripts/build_ffmpeg.py, scripts/generate_gn.py)

third_party/opus.what: libopus, linked statically into the library (FFmpeg's BUILD.gn depends on //third_party/opus), at Opus revision 55513e81d8f606bd75d0ff773d2144e5f2a732f5

tools/generate_stubs.what: the script BUILD.gn runs on Windows to write ffmpeg.def, the list of what ffmpeg.dll exports, from chromium/ffmpeg.sigs

third_party/nasm.what: the Netwide Assembler 3.01, which Chromium builds from source and BUILD.gn assembles FFmpeg's x86-64 assembly with on darwin-x64 and win-x64, through its nasm_assemble.gni

electron_ffmpeg.licence: LGPL-2.1-or-later (Chromium's FFmpeg as configured: no --enable-gpl, --enable-nonfree or --enable-version3), with libopus (BSD-3-Clause) linked statically inside it
